fit_combined_two_ways.note: Combines the largest-x beta with the mean fixed-ratio delta=alpha+beta, then fits C with those exponents. alpha_se combines marginal SEs in quadrature and ignores correlation; C residual SE is conditional on fitted exponents.

fit_fixed_x.note: Log-log OLS over all eight ratios; curvature in the ratio biases a pure power fit. Standard errors describe OLS residuals only.

fit_fixed_ratio.note: Top-level estimate is the mean of eight slopes; its SE is their dispersion/sqrt(8). By-ratio OLS SEs are reported separately. Fits hold the target ratio fixed; actual ratios differ because y is integral.

fit_joint.note: Joint unweighted OLS log V=log C+alpha log x+beta log f(y). This power-law C is distinct from the small-ratio asymptotic-normalisation intercept.

constant_extrapolated.method: Unweighted OLS z(r)=C+a*sqrt(r), using actual r=f(y)/x at the largest x and only target ratios at or above the stable cutoff. Uncertainty is max(2*intercept_SE, adjacent-cutoff shift, linear-in-r / quadratic-in-sqrt(r) model shifts, change on fitting the second-largest x); it is a sensitivity envelope, not a confidence interval. Functional form is empirical and not identified by these finite ratios.
constant_extrapolated.cutoff_sensitivity_note: The lower adjacent cutoff is unavailable when the chosen cutoff is 0.01, the bottom of the requested grid.

validation: g(q,l)/[6/pi^2] verified with exact Fraction arithmetic against complete finite-period sieves for all q <= 50 (1275 residue classes); sieved primes are 2,3 and all primes dividing q. The finite-period product is removed exactly.
Actual squarefree densities at x=1000000 checked for every q <= 50; maximum absolute |Q/x-g| = 3.17040894156e-05. This is a finite-density check, not an exact equality to the limiting density.

At x=1000 every selected modulus (union of all three polynomial sequences, including every odd q <= 999) was checked against direct integer Q counts and exact rational density coefficients. Maximum relative/absolute scaled double-double aggregation discrepancy 4.75e-32; cumulative V discrepancies < 1e-23 relative.

C++ checks sum_l Q(x;q,l)=Q(x;1,1) and sum_l Q^2 against direct counts for all q <= 50 at every production x, and for all 2 <= q <= 1000 at x=1000. Integer NTT zero lag equals Q(x;1,1), and every correlation coefficient satisfies 0 <= C(h) <= x-h. The NTT prime exceeds x, so modular coefficients lift uniquely to exact integer counts.

At the largest x=256000000, all 24 grid-endpoint per-modulus density aggregations were independently checked against exact Fraction arithmetic. Squarefree-divisibility counts were recomputed by an integer Mobius floor sum (150 distinct divisors). Maximum scaled discrepancy: 5.46e-32.
At x=1000000 the 24 grid-endpoint exact count sums were reproduced with an independent NTT prime/root (469762049,3), agreeing exactly with the production prime/root (3221225473,5).
notes: All Q and autocorrelation counts and weighted count-square sums are exact integers. Density rational coefficients are evaluated using double-double arithmetic (~31 decimal digits); 6/pi^2 and final V are evaluated with mpmath at 70 digits. V is not an integer or exact rational: V=A-2*x*(6/pi^2)*B+x^2*(6/pi^2)^2*D. Decimal strings are rounded to 20 significant digits, conservatively below the roughly 31-digit double-double working precision to allow for accumulation and cancellation; small-x values are independently checked against exact rational arithmetic. All grid y are the largest integers with f(y)<=target_ratio*x. No paper, website or external source was consulted. Normalised values have persistent dependence on the ratio across the x grid, so fixed-x slopes can absorb ratio curvature. Stability can be nonmonotone in ratio; the cutoff requires every higher grid row to pass. Fits are empirical and their OLS SEs do not account for finite-x bias, ratio curvature, polynomial sampling, or extrapolation misspecification. Adjacent lower-cutoff fits are sensitivity diagnostics and may intentionally include an unstable row; the central fit excludes all rows below its cutoff.
